Previews (scratch QA only): python3 /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/steam/logo_work/preview.py writes prev_*.png to scratchpad/steam/logo_work/previews/, each logo composited on dark, bright, busy (title-screen crop) and checkerboard backgrounds.
notes: How it is built: the logo lines use the real GradientText widget with UiTheme.font(F.LOGO) (Orbitron 900). The tagline is the same Label as title_screen.gd: FontVariation of F.TITLE (Exo 2 800 italic), UiTheme.theme() applied, cyan text, pink 60% shadow. Every title-screen number is multiplied by 6: logo font 480 px, outline 60, shadow (30,30), line step 504; tagline 162 px, glyph spacing 30, shadow (12,12), shadow outline 6 (the theme default of 1, scaled). Line-to-tagline spacing is the same as on the title screen. Colours and gradient come straight from the GradientText shader.

Glyph sharpness: the fonts are dynamic (no MSDF, oversampling 0 = auto, fixed_size 0) and every SubViewport sets oversampling_override = 1.0, so FreeType rasterises the glyphs at the full 480 px. I checked this in the output: edges have a 1 px anti-aliasing transition and the outline is a clean 15 px ring (Godot draws about outline/4).

Premultiplied-alpha fix: a transparent Godot SubViewport stores premultiplied colour, so saving it directly would darken the 85% cyan shadow to about (35,184,208) at the edges. A final shader pass with render_mode blend_disabled divides by alpha and writes straight alpha. Verified values in the PNG: shadow (41,216,245) at alpha 233 and 108, ink outline #1A0533, tagline #29D8F5, tagline shadow #FF2E88 at alpha 153. Image.fix_alpha_edges() also puts the edge colour under almost-transparent pixels. Pillow resamples RGBA premultiplied (tested), so downscaling produces no dark halos.

Checked: no clipped glyphs or shadows (256 px render margin; the outermost padding rows are alpha 0); no outline gaps; no dark fringes on a bright background. Every file was viewed directly and composited on dark, bright, busy and checkerboard backgrounds.

Glow (_glow files): two gaussians, sigma 18 and 60 px at master scale (3 and 10 px at title-screen scale), weights 0.35 and 0.5. Pink around CROSSING/EUROPE, cyan around the tagline, about 35-40% alpha at the outline, fading over about 130 px. It is blurred on the GPU at quarter resolution; alpha below 2/255 is cut. The glow sits behind the logo, so it shows faintly through the translucent cyan shadow rim, the same as an outer glow in Photoshop.

Viewer warning: some viewers drop alpha on large PNGs (the Read tool did for logo_stacked_center_glow.png) and show the glow files as a solid pink/cyan block with a stepped edge on black. That is only the straight RGB under near-zero alpha. Composited properly the glow is soft; see glow_alpha_check.png and the prev_*glow*.png previews.

Monogram: it is about 1.85:1, not roughly square. Orbitron's C and E are wide, and the only ways to make CE square (stretching, stacking or overlapping the letters) would distort the brand font and read worse at small sizes. In a test icon, side-by-side CE across a square background reads clearly at 128, 64 and 32 px and is still recognisable at 16 px. Suggestion for the icon compositor: place it horizontally centred at about 85% of the icon width over the sun/grid and pad to square.

logo_wide keeps the tagline at title-screen size, about 40% of the line width. With the logo about 650 px wide in a 920x430 capsule the tagline glyphs are roughly 19 px tall. If that is too small, use logo_stacked_center there.

This renders all five finals (portrait, landscape, hero, icon_bg, portrait_b) into /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/steam/scene. Use --out DIR or $STEAM_SCENE_OUT to write elsewhere.

Render time on this machine (Cycles CPU, 3 threads) is about 27 min in total:
- car build: about 25 s, once per run
- portrait: 5.7 min (128 samples)
- landscape: 3.5 min (128 samples)
- hero: 9.1 min (96 samples)
- icon_bg: 1.0 min (64 samples)
- portrait_b: 6.2 min (128 samples)
- post-processing: 5-23 s per image
The first full pass took 1607.7 s; portrait_b was then re-rendered with the current settings (front lights and road specular tuned) in 371 s. The current script reproduces all five.

Other options:
- One shot only: --shots hero (comma-separated list).
- Quick previews: --scale 0.25 renders all five in about 1 min and writes <shot>_pv.png.
- Full-resolution detail check of a region: --crop x0,y0,x1,y1 (fractions, y measured from the top).
- Override samples: --samples N.
- Keep the linear renders: --keep-exr --exr-dir DIR.
- Re-run only the post (bloom, vignette, left-side darkening, tone, dither) on kept EXRs: --post-only --exr-dir DIR. The 32-bit EXRs of the current finals are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/steam/work/exr_final (121 MB). For example, add --post-only --exr-dir <that dir> to the command above to rebuild all PNGs in about 1 min; this was verified to be bit-identical.

The post parameters per shot are in SHOTS[shot]['post']; the defaults are in post().
notes: Car: the game's real Sportwagen. The script builds it with cesprites.rig.Rig plus player_cars.build(), using the catalog.player_sets() params for 'player/sportwagen' (paint #cc1419, metal 0.15).

Car lights: each car material's CE_PASS switch (Mix of BSDF or layer emission) is rewired to BSDF + emission, with the pass group set to base=1, tail=12, brake=0.3. The lamp internals (rings, light guides, fills) glow through the red lenses, which keep their base tinted-transparent look. The plate lamp is dimmed and the reflectors only catch light. portrait_b also lights the headlight DRL and projector.

Mirror fix: in the model, the door-mirror arms float about 11 cm above the body shoulder (confirmed by ray casts). This is invisible in the small game sprites but obvious in close-ups. The scene script moves the mirror assemblies 7 cm inward and 7.5 cm down. No game code or assets were changed.

Scene, sky: one world shader holds the sky gradient (navy, purple, magenta horizon), the warm halo and two stepped halo rings, the striped retro sun (yellow #FFF59E, orange #FF8F29, pink #FF2E87) and screen-pixel-sized stars. Because the sun is in the world shader it always sits on the horizon behind everything.

Scene, ridges: three low-poly ridges, dark purple with emissive crest lines and soft glow ribbons: pink on the far ridge, violet in the middle, cyan on the near ridge. Their height is set per shot and lower on the logo side.

Scene, floor and road: the endless floor has a magenta grid whose lines are filtered by pixel footprint, so it has no aliasing and merges into a pink band at the horizon, with haze matched to the sky. The road has two 3.75 m lanes, cyan edge lines and a yellow dashed centre line.

Speed cue: Cycles motion blur. The camera, the car and its lights move together 1.1 m during the shutter, so the near road dashes and grid lines streak, the rims spin and the car stays sharp. There is no police car; the car stays the only focal point.

Lighting: the warm sun lamp shines from the sun's direction as diffuse light only. With glossy reflections on, its highlights were about 1000x brighter than the painted sun, which blew out the road in the first test. Reflections therefore show the painted sun, grid and neon. The car is lit by pink and cyan strip lights along its flanks, a pink kicker on the rear quarter and a dim violet fill. A warm top light was removed for the rear views because it put a white bar on the rear window.

Colour handling: the post-processing in numpy, working from linear EXR, replaces Blender's view transform with a Standard-like sRGB transform plus a soft per-channel shoulder. This keeps the pink and cyan as saturated as on the title screen; AgX or Filmic would wash them out. It also adds a 4-scale bloom, a vignette and a ±1 LSB dither against banding in the dark sky.
Render quality: Cycles CPU with adaptive sampling (threshold 0.015, 32-128 samples), the OpenImageDenoise denoiser (accurate prefilter), indirect clamp 3 and filter glossy 0.7.

QA, done on every final with Read plus 100% crops: there is no visible noise. An isolated-peak test found only glints on the exhaust tips and plate lettering (0-7 px per image), so there are no fireflies. Near-white pixels are at most 0.005%, except portrait_b at 0.13% from the headlight cores. Paint clips only in neon highlights (median R about 180 of 255). The camera has no roll, so all horizons are straight, and the car is fully in frame in every shot.
Positions below are fractions of width and height, with y measured from the top. Car positions come from object bounding boxes, so they are slightly generous.

portrait framing: 38 mm lens, camera 1.85 m high and about 4.4 m behind the bumper. The vanishing point and horizon are at (0.50, 0.57). The sun's centre is at (0.50, 0.48) with a radius of 0.27 of the width, and its top is at y 0.30. The car spans x 0.42-0.93 and y 0.63-0.85: right lane, yaw 8° nose-left (a lane change), seen from behind and slightly above. That is about half the image width, roughly 70-78 px at a 150 px thumbnail.

notes: Portrait background: portrait.png, not portrait_b.png. portrait.png is the title-screen composition: the car seen from behind with its rear wing, heading into the striped sun, with road leading lines, yellow dashes and the grid. It fills the lower half and still reads at 150x225. portrait_b leaves its bottom third as empty dark road, the front of the car is less recognisable, and at 150x225 the car shrinks to a small blob in front of the sun (compared side by side at 600x900, 300x450 and 150x225). To switch, set PORTRAIT bg='portrait_b.png', top=0.06; the layout check knows its sun and car boxes.

Logo variant: logo_stacked_center_glow on BOTH capsules, so both carry the same lockup and treatment. At 1:1 the glow makes the logo look lit like the bloomed sun and neon instead of pasted on. It does not soften legibility at 150x225 (compared with the plain version). Portrait: CROSSING glyphs are 86% of the width, frame at y 0.050-0.272. The sky is calm until the sun top at 0.30, so the tagline sits in the sun's magenta halo with good cyan contrast. No scrim was needed.

Landscape: the stacked lockup, not logo_wide. In the free left ~47% the wide lockup's cap height would be ~6 px at 230x107; the stacked one gives ~12 px. CROSSING glyph width is 40% of the canvas, glyphs start at x 0.05, frame x 0.050-0.454 / y 0.094-0.425 (sun starts at x 0.53, car at 0.61). Top-left placement mirrors the title screen and keeps the tagline off the bright horizon band; I rejected a mid-height version where it sat on that band. A 0.30 elliptical scrim with compact support dims the ridge neon lines behind EUROPE and the tagline. No pixel outside its ellipse changes, and it does not read as a dark blob.

Hero: a pass-through as required, with no logo and no text. The @2x file is bit-identical to scene/hero.png; the @1x is a 2x Lanczos downscale. The contact sheet mock-up assumes Steam places logo.png at the bottom left over the calm left side, where it reads well.

Logo files: logo.png is an exact crop of logo_wide.png to its alpha bounds (5358x602), with untouched pixels, so the logo agent's verified colours and alpha edges are kept. logo_1280x720.png is the wide lockup at 1152 px (90% width) centred on the canvas. It was resampled with premultiplied alpha and has the colour bled into fully transparent pixels: 0 of 822,617 transparent pixels are black.

Icon, detailed design (512, 256 and ICO 48/64/128/256): CE glyphs at 84% width, centred at y 0.71, so the sun cap with its first stripe shows above the letters. Below the horizon the ground fades toward 45% brightness, which calms the grid and road lines inside the letter counters while the sun and the glowing horizon stay untouched. I rejected an elliptical scrim here because it dimmed the sun into a muddy brown.

Icon, small sizes (ICO 16/24/32): the detailed design turned to mush at 24 and 16 px, mainly because the baked-in cyan shadow fills the letter counters. The simplified variant has the ground calmed to 18% below the horizon, the CE glyphs with the baked shadow removed, and a separate pixel-aligned cyan shadow (1 px at 24/32 px, none at 16 px; with one at 16 px the counters fill up again). It also adds a heavier ink outline (+0.5 px). It is composed on a 16x master and reduced with an exact box filter. The glyph width (84-90%) and sub-pixel offset are searched for the sharpest edges. Result: 'CE' reads at 32 and 24 px and is still legible at 16 px.

Compositing method: all maths in float32, in sRGB-encoded space (the same space Godot's 2D canvas blends in). Layers are premultiplied on load; Lanczos runs per channel on 32-bit float with the overshoot clamped (alpha to [0,1], colour to [0,alpha]); compositing uses premultiplied 'over'. The @1x files are downscaled from the float @2x composite. Opaque files are 8-bit RGB with a seeded TPDF dither applied only to values that are not exact 8-bit levels, so pixels the compositor did not touch stay bit-identical. Transparent files are 8-bit RGBA with straight alpha. A 4x zoom of the logo edges at @2x and @1x shows no dark or light fringes and no banding in the glow.

All PNGs are 8-bit, non-interlaced, without iCCP/gAMA/cHRM chunks (so treated as sRGB), have valid CRCs and contain no text metadata. All opaque assets are RGB without an alpha channel.

Each 1x file matches a Lanczos downscale of its 2x version (PSNR 52+ dB, max difference 8-15). hero_3840x1240 is bit-identical to scene/hero.png. No 1-pixel border seams on any asset. No banding or fireflies even with a strong gamma boost; residual noise on the dark road is about 0.5 levels.

logo.png is tightly cropped: visible pixels touch all four edges (bounding box at alpha 1 or more equals the full 5358x602 canvas). The alpha is clean, with no haze: no visible pixel lies more than 20 px from solid glyph pixels. There are no dark or white fringes when composited on white, grey, dark navy or a checkerboard, and a straight-alpha resample changes only 141 of 46k pixels by more than 30 levels.

logo_1280x720.png is exactly 1280x720 and the logo is centred to within 0.5 px (visible box 62..1217 x 292..426). Colour is bled under alpha 0 (no black pixels there), 89% of the canvas is fully transparent, and no visible pixel lies more than 6 px from the glyphs.

Spelling is correct on every asset: 'CROSSING EUROPE' and 'A RACING XPERIENCE'. The brand look matches the title screen: Orbitron gradient with the light band, #1A0533 outline, a two-step cyan offset shadow structured like the in-game rendering, and the cyan Exo 2 italic tagline with pink shadow.

Safe margins pass. Portrait logo: about 6.2-7.4% at the sides and 4.8-5.3% at the top. Landscape logo outline: about 5.0% left and 9.9% top. The portrait title reads clearly at 150x225 and the tagline is still legible; the landscape title reads at 230x107. The car is never cut off (landscape wing ends at about x=850 of 920).

The hero has no logo and no overlay text; the only text is the licence plate 'S-CE 455', which matches the in-game car. The car sits at 63-86% of the width and 43-72% of the height, the sun at 51-69% of the width. The left 40% holds only dark sky, mountains and grid. The bottom 24% is empty dark road, which suits Steam's bottom fade. A simulated default bottom-left overlay of logo.png reads well.

icon.ico holds 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 128 and 256 px frames, all 32-bit, PNG-compressed and fully opaque, and all read back with PIL. The 256 frame matches icon_256.png (max difference 2). The simplified 16/24/32 px frames are clearly crisper than a plain downscale of the 512 design, and the 'CE' with the sun is recognisable even at 16 px.
File sizes are modest: grids 0.4-1.9 MB, hero 1.0 and 3.7 MB, logos 221 and 367 KB, ICO 108 KB.

issues.asset: grid_portrait_600x900 / 1200x1800, grid_landscape_920x430 / 1840x860, hero_1920x620 / 3840x1240 (scene renders portrait.png, landscape.png, hero.png)
issues.problem: Between the horizon and the car, the road shows as a muddy brown/olive smear. Sampled colours: portrait road (82,47,40), hue ~10°; landscape left of the car (68,40,32), hue ~13°; hero near the vanishing point (98,32,36). That is about 5% of the portrait, all of it around the car, which is the focal subject. The title-screen road is deep indigo (14,6,39), hue 255°. Brown is not in the palette, so the key art looks dirty and the red car loses contrast. Cause: the glossy asphalt (road_spec 0.28, roughness 0.42-0.62 driven by the 0.35-scale 'patches' noise) reflects the warm sun and sunset glow as cloudy brown patches, and the warm horizon haze adds to it near the vanishing point.
issues.fix: In keyart_scene.py road_material: set road_spec 0.28 -> 0.12 for portrait, landscape and hero (portrait_b already uses 0.1). Replace the patches roughness map with a constant 0.5 and shift the asphalt mix toward violet (#0a0811/#17131f -> #0c0718/#170d2c). Optionally change the broad sunset glow from #ff6a3d to #ff3d7a. Re-render the three shots (about 18 min total going by final_render.log) and recompose. Acceptance: the road between horizon and car averages hue 260-330° with V <= 0.20, and pixels with hue <45°, S 0.25-0.75 and V 0.12-0.45 make up less than 0.5% of the portrait.

issues.problem: The logo lockup sits on the mountain ridges instead of in clear sky. The far ridge's pink crest (peak at y ~0.29 at x ~0.14) rises behind the bottom of 'EUROPE' and crosses the tagline. The violet peaks sit right under 'A RACING', and the cyan crest runs only ~15 px under the cyan tagline. The 0.30 scrim dims these lines but does not remove them. The result is text over neon line work, which looks cluttered and breaks the title-screen layout, where the whole lockup sits in sky above the ridges.
issues.fix: Re-render the landscape with ridge_scale 0.85 -> 0.6 and ridge_tilt 0.35 -> 0.8. Check in a --scale 0.25 preview that no crest line rises above y = 0.40 left of x = 0.47. Then in compose.py LANDSCAPE set cy 0.26 -> 0.225 and body_w 0.40 -> 0.37, which puts the frame at roughly y 0.07-0.38 with clear sky under the tagline. While re-composing, use logo_stacked_left (left-aligned, as on the title screen) instead of the centred stack.

issues.problem: The Steam logo is the one-line 8.9:1 lockup, not the stacked CROSSING / EUROPE layout of the title screen. Steam fits the logo into its pinned bottom-left box, so a strip this wide becomes thin: the tagline ends up ~13 px tall on a 1920 hero and ~9 px on a Steam Deck. logo_1280x720 uses only 19% of the canvas height (visible area 1156x135), so if someone picks that file in Steam the logo shrinks further.
issues.fix: Ship the stacked, left-aligned lockup (logo/logo_stacked_left.png, about 2.4:1, same layout as the title screen) as logo.png, and keep the wide one as logo_wide.png for anyone who prefers it. Recompose logo_1280x720 from the stacked lockup, width-limited at 90% (~1150x480, about 67% of the canvas height), and update the game-page mock-up in the contact sheet.

issues.problem: The top of the sun is only 6.8% below the top edge (sun_top 0.068 in the render log). The brief says Steam may crop the top, and even a small crop would flatten the disc, the brightest element in the image. It also sits uncomfortably close to the edge.
issues.fix: For the hero, set sun elev 3.5 -> 3.0 and rho 6.0 -> 5.3. That puts the top at ~8.3° elevation, ~12.5% below the top edge, and still lets the car's wing overlap the lower stripes. Re-render together with the road fix.

issues.problem: The upper half of the sun is a nearly flat pale cream: the portrait top samples (255,249,178), and R is pinned at 255 down to the middle (255,195,115). SUN_TOP reuses the logo's #FFF59E, and the per-channel shoulder then compresses R and G together. The title-screen sun is clearly more saturated: (255,224,102) -> (255,184,74) -> (255,132,65). In the portrait, the sun and the logo's identical pale-yellow tops compete for attention.
issues.fix: In keyart_scene.py, set SUN_TOP #fff59e -> #ffe066 (the title-screen sun) and lower the sun's emission by ~20%, so after post the top lands near (255,225,110) and the middle near (255,165,70). Keep the bloom and halo as they are.

issues.problem: The car spans x 0.42-0.93 and ends at y 0.85, so the bottom 15% is nearly empty dark asphalt. The sun (52% wide and the brightest element) takes the centre. For a racing game, the car could carry more weight at 150-200 px library width.
issues.fix: Dolly the portrait camera in ~0.5 m (loc y -6.6 -> -6.1) and move it ~0.3 m right (x 1.25 -> 1.55), keeping lens and vanish so the horizon, sun and logo layout stay put. The car should grow ~12% with its bumper at ~0.89 height and the wing tip at least 5% from the right edge. Check car_x / car_y in the render log of a --scale 0.25 preview.

issues.problem: The floor grid reads as horizontal stripes. With 1.1 m of motion-blur travel, the near lateral lines smear into soft, wide magenta bars that stop abruptly at the road edge (hero x 0-40%, y 0.50-0.65). Because the camera is so low, the longitudinal lines run almost flat, so the crisp converging grid of the title screen is lost. This busy pattern, plus the cyan edge line that touches the 'C' in the game-page mock-up, falls exactly where Steam pins the logo.
issues.fix: For hero and landscape, set motion 1.1 -> 0.5 (the dashes still streak), and strengthen the logo-side darkening: hero post left_dark (0.2, 0.45) -> (0.32, 0.5). If the stacked logo is adopted, re-check the mock-up so the logo sits over dark road and not over the bars or the cyan line.

strengths: The logo matches the game's GradientText exactly because it was rendered with Godot: Orbitron Black, #FFF59E -> #FF8F29 -> #FF2E87 gradient with the light band, #1A0533 outline, and the same two-step cyan shadow (solid core plus a lower-alpha outer band). The Exo 2 italic tagline has the pink shadow. Pixels under partial alpha are ink, cyan or pink, never black or white, so there are no halos or fringes on the logo PNGs or the composites.

The portrait capsule reads very well at library size. 'CROSSING EUROPE' is still legible at 120 px wide, the car and sun read clearly at 150-200 px, and the hierarchy runs cleanly from logo to sun to car.

Rendering is clean: no fireflies, flat-area high-pass noise std is 0.4-2.6, and an 8x contrast stretch of the dark road and sky shows no banding (thanks to the dither). The Lanczos downscales show no ringing at the sun edge or the logo outline.

The hero follows Steam's rules: no logo or text, the car stays out of the left 45%, and the red Sportwagen's dark wing is silhouetted against the striped sun right of centre. It sits well in the game-page mock-up.

The synthwave look is consistent with the title screen: striped retro sun, layered purple ridges with pink, violet and cyan crest lines, magenta grid, cyan road edges, yellow dashes, and the in-game red Sportwagen with its rear wing. The German 'S-CE 455' plate is a nice touch, and the magenta logo glow ties the logo into the scene without muddying it.
The CE monogram icon uses the brand style, and the 16, 24 and 32 px frames are tuned separately, so the monogram still reads at 32 px. The ICO contains all seven sizes and is fully opaque.

Technically correct: exact pixel sizes, consistent @2x variants, opaque RGB for the grids, hero and icons, RGBA for the logos, logo.png cropped exactly to its alpha bounds, and a useful QA contact sheet with Steam-size thumbnails and an ICO zoom.

open_issues: Deviation from the art review's road numbers: I used roughness 0.75 instead of the suggested constant 0.5, plus a slightly bluer asphalt (#0e0a26/#1a1240 instead of #0c0718/#170d2c). Half-scale tests showed 0.5 still mirrors the sun as a warm sheen at the portrait's grazing angles (brown share 4.0%); lowering the specular alone barely helps because of Fresnel. 0.75 plus the bluer asphalt meets the acceptance criteria (hue 260-330°, V <= 0.20, < 0.5% brown).

The portrait dash_gain of 1.7 was not in the review. I added it because after the road fix the remaining 'brown' pixels were the bloom halo of the large near dashes, not the asphalt. The landscape and hero keep 2.2 and pass the criterion anyway.

Sun colour: the top lands on target at (252,219,126). The disc centre reads (253,142,107), bluer than the review's (255,165,70), because the sky's pink halo, which I kept as instructed, adds blue inside the disc.

Hero plus logo mock-up: Steam's exact default logo box is not documented; I assumed bottom-left, about 50% x 50%. In that box the stacked logo's CROSSING line overlaps the horizon and grid band, and the left cyan road edge passes between CROSSING and EUROPE. EUROPE and the tagline sit on dark road. It reads cleanly thanks to the ink outline and the calmer, darker grid. With this composition the road edge always crosses the bottom left. Users can shrink or move the logo in Steam.

The German Steam menu labels in the README ('Ein Nicht-Steam-Spiel hinzufügen', 'Verwalten' -> 'Eigenes Artwork festlegen', 'Eigenen Hintergrund festlegen', 'Eigenes Logo festlegen', 'Eigenschaften') follow the brief. I could not check them against a live German client. The README notes that labels may differ slightly by Steam version and describes the logo-position adjustment neutrally.

result.how_to_rebuild:
Run from the repo root /home/user/crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience:
(1) Logo lockups (Godot 4.7.2, about 15 s; writes 7 PNGs to /tmp/crossing-europe-steam/logo, or pass -- --out=DIR):
xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1280x720x24" godot --path . --rendering-driver opengl3 --audio-driver Dummy -s res://tools/steam/render_logo.gd
(2) Scene renders (Blender 5.2 bpy, Cycles CPU, about 18 min at 4 threads; writes portrait/landscape/hero/icon_bg to /tmp/crossing-europe-steam/scene, or pass --out DIR):
CE_THREADS=4 /home/user/tools/bpyenv/bin/python tools/steam/keyart_scene.py --shots portrait,landscape,hero,icon_bg
Add --keep-exr --exr-dir DIR to allow post-only reruns. --scale 0.25 gives about 1-min previews.
(3) Compose (python3 + Pillow + numpy, about 20 s; reads the two folders above or --logo-dir/--scene-dir, writes the whole set plus .gdignore into marketing/steam/, or pass --out DIR):
python3 tools/steam/compose.py
To rebuild the current finals exactly without re-rendering:
python3 tools/steam/compose.py --logo-dir /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/steam/final_work/logo --scene-dir /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/steam/final_work/scene
The scene PNGs can be regenerated bit-identically from the kept EXRs:
keyart_scene.py --post-only --exr-dir /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-crossing-europe---a-racing-xperience/3a945943-d653-5a54-8279-676b9bc6f9e5/scratchpad/steam/final_work/exr --out DIR
Layout knobs: PORTRAIT/LANDSCAPE/ICON/SMALL/LOGO in compose.py. Scene knobs: SHOTS, ASPHALT, ROAD_SPEC, ROAD_ROUGH, SUN_TOP, SUN_GAIN in keyart_scene.py.
